You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To make candied citrus, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Slice the citrus into uniform rounds (10 minutes)
Step 2. Simmer the slices in the sugar syrup (45 minutes)
Step 3. Prepare a cooling rack over a baking sheet (5 minutes)
Step 4. Transfer slices to the cooling rack (10 minutes)
Step 5. Measure the granulated sugar for coating (2 minutes)
Step 6. Wash the citrus fruit thoroughly (5 minutes)
Step 7. Select the freshest oranges and lemons (5 minutes)
Step 8. Sterilize the storage jars (15 minutes)
Step 9. Allow the candied slices to cool completely (3 hours)
Step 10. Label the jars with the date (2 minutes)
Step 11. Zest one extra fruit for garnish (5 minutes)
Step 12. Combine sugar and water in a large pot (5 minutes)
Step 13. Place jars in the pantry (2 minutes)
Step 14. Sharpen the paring knife (10 minutes)
Step 15. Dry the jars with a lint-free towel (5 minutes)
Step 16. Clear the workspace on the counter (10 minutes)
Step 17. Blanch the citrus slices to remove bitterness (12 minutes)
Step 18. Set aside the citrus peels for other uses (5 minutes)
Step 19. Sift the coating sugar to remove lumps (3 minutes)
Step 20. Boil the sugar syrup until it reaches a simmer (8 minutes)
Step 21. Check the temperature of the syrup with a thermometer (1 minute)
Step 22. Organize the final packaging materials (10 minutes)
Step 23. Skim the foam off the top of the syrup (5 minutes)
Step 24. Lay out parchment paper (2 minutes)
Step 25. Weigh the sugar for the syrup (3 minutes)
Step 26. Remove seeds from the citrus slices (15 minutes)
Step 27. Juice the remaining fruit halves (10 minutes)
Step 28. Whisk the syrup to ensure even melting (2 minutes)
Step 29. Store excess juice in the refrigerator (2 minutes)
Step 30. Prepare a sugar dusting station (5 minutes)
Step 31. Wipe down the stove surface (5 minutes)
Step 32. Gather all necessary ingredients and tools (10 minutes)
Step 33. Adjust the heat to maintain a low boil (2 minutes)
Step 34. Inspect the citrus for any bruises (3 minutes)
Step 35. Toss the slices in extra sugar (20 minutes)
Step 36. Compost the citrus ends (2 minutes)
Step 37. Set out a cutting board (1 minute)
Step 38. Pack the candied citrus into jars (15 minutes)
Step 39. Measure the corn syrup to prevent crystallization (2 minutes)
Step 40. Inspect the slices for translucency (5 minutes)
Step 41. Clean the measuring cups (5 minutes)
Step 42. Cut the slices into smaller wedges if desired (10 minutes)
Step 43. Arrange the slices so they do not overlap (10 minutes)
Step 44. Pat the raw slices dry with paper towels (10 minutes)
Step 45. Let the sugar coating set (1 hour)
Step 46. Rinse the citrus slices in cold water (2 minutes)
Step 47. Seal the jars tightly (1 minute)
Step 48. Check the syrup for a thick consistency (5 minutes)
Step 49. Clean the citrus juicer (5 minutes)
Step 50. Calibrate the kitchen scale (2 minutes)
Step 51. Drain the slices from the blanching water (3 minutes)
Step 52. Measure the water volume for the syrup (2 minutes)
Step 53. Reduce the syrup volume by half (20 minutes)
Step 54. Verify the sugar-to-water ratio (2 minutes)
Step 55. Grate a small amount of ginger for flavor (5 minutes)
Step 56. Remove stems from the fruit (2 minutes)
Step 57. Prepare a bowl of ice water (4 minutes)
Step 58. Final quality check of the slices (5 minutes)
Step 59. Wash the colander (3 minutes)
Step 60. Prepare a tray for the finished product (5 minutes)
Step 61. Check the pantry for backup sugar (2 minutes)
Step 62. Dip the edges of the slices in chocolate (30 minutes)
Step 63. Dry the juicer components (5 minutes)
Step 64. Clean the prep bowls (10 minutes)
Step 65. Dissolve the sugar completely in the water (10 minutes)
Step 66. Set the kitchen timer (30 seconds)
Step 67. Cut a piece of waxed paper (1 minute)
Step 68. Place the pot on the burner (30 seconds)
Step 69. Reserve a cup of the flavored syrup (5 minutes)
Step 70. Put away the sugar container (2 minutes)
Step 71. Add a splash of vanilla extract (1 minute)
Step 72. Sanitize the countertop (10 minutes)
Step 73. Shake off excess sugar (5 minutes)
Step 74. Let the chocolate-dipped slices harden (45 minutes)
Step 75. Strain the syrup through a fine-mesh sieve (5 minutes)
Step 76. Tie ribbons around the jars for gifting (15 minutes)
Step 77. Clean the syrup pot (15 minutes)
Step 78. Test a slice for tenderness (2 minutes)
Step 79. Bring a fresh pot of water to a boil (10 minutes)
Step 80. Decorate the jar lids (20 minutes)
Step 81. Place slices in a single layer on a drying mat (5 minutes)
Step 82. Sort the citrus by size (5 minutes)
Step 83. Sweep the kitchen floor (10 minutes)
Step 84. Refill the sugar canister (3 minutes)
Step 85. Lay out a clean apron (1 minute)
Step 86. Sterilize the tongs (5 minutes)
Step 87. Cut the citrus into thin rings (15 minutes)
Step 88. Melt the dark chocolate in a double boiler (10 minutes)
Step 89. Pour the reserved syrup into a small bottle (2 minutes)
Step 90. Prepare the final display plate (5 minutes)
Step 91. Zest the fruit for an aromatic boost (5 minutes)
Step 92. Prepare the dredging bowl (3 minutes)
Step 93. Wipe the outside of the syrup bottle (1 minute)
Step 94. Remove any remaining seeds with a toothpick (10 minutes)
Step 95. Measure the citric acid (1 minute)
Step 96. Let the slices air dry overnight (12 hours)
Step 97. Re-heat the syrup if it thickens too much (5 minutes)
Step 98. Take a photo of the finished citrus (2 minutes)
Step 99. Discard the citrus peels (1 minute)
Step 100. Inspect the fruit for ripeness (2 minutes)
